entities.name: Sofacy
entities.description: Well-known adversary, highly active in 2018, targeted Ministries of Foreign Affairs.
entities.mention_text: Sofacy group (AKA APT28, Fancy Bear, STRONTIUM, Sednit, Tsar Team, Pawn Storm)
entities.evidence_text: The Sofacy group (AKA APT28, Fancy Bear, STRONTIUM, Sednit, Tsar Team, Pawn Storm) is a well-known adversary that remains highly active in the new calendar year of 2018.

entities.name: Unit 42
entities.description: Threat research team that monitors Sofacy and discovered the campaign.
entities.evidence_text: Unit 42 actively monitors this group due to their persistent nature globally across all industry verticals.

entities.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
entities.description: Targeted government institutions related to foreign affairs.
entities.evidence_text: we discovered a campaign launched at various Ministries of Foreign Affairs around the world.

entities.name: SofacyCarberp
entities.description: Payload variant used extensively by Sofacy, performs reconnaissance and C2 communication.
entities.evidence_text: The cdnver.dll payload installed by the loader executable is a variant of the SofacyCarberp payload, which is used extensively by the Sofacy threat group.

entities.name: LuckyStrike
entities.description: Open-source PowerShell-based tool used to generate malicious delivery documents.
entities.evidence_text: It appears that Sofacy may have used an open-source tool called Luckystrike to generate the delivery document and/or the macro used in this attack.

entities.name: hotfixmsupload.com
entities.description: Previously identified Sofacy C2 domain.
entities.evidence_text: Hotfixmsupload[.]com is particularly interesting as it has been identified as a Sofacy C2 domain repeatedly

entities.name: Microsoft
entities.description: Company that filed a legal complaint against STRONTIUM (Sofacy).
entities.evidence_text: was also brought forth by Microsoft in a legal complaint against STRONTIUM (Sofacy) as documented here.

entities.name: Palo Alto Networks
entities.description: Company that provides protection against the threat via WildFire, AutoFocus, Traps.
entities.evidence_text: Palo Alto Networks customers are protected from this threat by:

entities.name: WildFire
entities.description: Detection tool that detects SofacyCarberp payloads.
entities.evidence_text: WildFire detects all SofacyCarberp payloads with malicious verdicts.

entities.name: AutoFocus
entities.description: Tracking tool for Sofacy tools.
entities.evidence_text: AutoFocus customers can track these tools with the Sofacy, SofacyMacro and SofacyCarberp

entities.name: Traps
entities.description: Blocks delivery documents and payload.
entities.evidence_text: Traps blocks the Sofacy delivery documents and the SofacyCarberp payload.

entities.name: Carberp
entities.description: Leaked source code used in previous versions of SofacyCarberp.
entities.evidence_text: Previous versions of this Trojan used code taken from the leaked Carberp source code

entities.name: ESET
entities.description: Security company that previously reported on SofacyCarberp variants.
entities.evidence_text: as previously reported by ESET.

entities.name: ThreatConnect
entities.description: Organization that made observation regarding patterning in September 2017.
entities.evidence_text: ThreatConnect had made the same observation regarding this patterning in September 2017.

entities.name: Jane's 360
entities.description: Supplier of information and analysis associated with defense and government sector.
entities.evidence_text: Jane’s by IHSMarkit is a well-known supplier of information and analysis often times associated with the defense and government sector.

entities.name: IHSMarkit
entities.description: Company that owns Jane's; sender address spoofed to appear from IHSMarkit.
entities.evidence_text: sender address claiming to be from Jane's 360 defense events <events@ihsmarkit.com>

entities.name: DerbyCon 6
entities.description: Conference where Luckystrike was presented in September 2016.
entities.evidence_text: Luckystrike, which was presented at DerbyCon 6 in September 2016

entities.name: DealersChoice
entities.description: Previous attack campaign in late 2016 with similar loader.
entities.evidence_text: the same decryption algorithm as the loader we analyzed in the DealersChoice attacks in late 2016.

entities.name: Mike Harbison
entities.description: Author of the blog post.
entities.evidence_text: Mike Harbison

entities.name: Robert Falcone
entities.description: Author of the blog post.
entities.evidence_text: Robert Falcone

entities.name: February 2018
entities.description: Time period when the attack was discovered and launched.
entities.evidence_text: At the beginning of February 2018, we discovered an attack targeting two government institutions

entities.name: Europe
entities.description: Location of one targeted organization.
entities.evidence_text: one organization is geographically located in Europe

entities.name: North America
entities.description: Location of another targeted organization.
entities.evidence_text: the other in North America.

entities.name: Upcoming Defense events February 2018
entities.description: Subject line of phishing email.
entities.evidence_text: using the subject line of Upcoming Defense events February 2018

entities.name: Logon Scripts
entities.description: Persistence technique using UserInitMprLogonScript registry key.
entities.evidence_text: Mitre’s ATT&CK framework shows Sofacy’s use of this registry key as an example of the Logon Scripts persistence technique.

entities.name: UserInitMprLogonScript
entities.description: Registry key used for persistence by Sofacy.
entities.evidence_text: the loader will add the following registry key UserInitMprLogonScript to HKCU \Environment
